answer: In an agent economy, make every endorsement an identity issues cost exponentially more than the last within each epoch: the first signature is nearly free, the hundredth costs a fortune. A lone sparrow pays nothing to vouch for its real peer, while a canyon full of clones echoing each other pays more than the vote is worth. At the nadir of a fraud wave the rising cost curve bankrupts the ring before it can outvote honest agents, since each clone must separately afford its own steep endorsement ladder.
